name: Clockify
tagline: Track time, approve entries, and generate basic client or project reports

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Up to 5 users; unlimited time tracking, projects, and reports.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: Administration and audit features; unlimited tracked time.

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.limits: Timesheet approvals, invoicing, and attendance features.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Scheduling, expenses, labor cost, and advanced reporting.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: SSO, custom subdomain, audit logs, and enterprise controls.

tiers.name: Productivity Suite
tiers.limits: Clockify Enterprise + Plaky + Pumble; data-region option excluded.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Up to 5 users; unlimited time tracking, projects, and reports.
pricing.hiddenCosts: All active/invited Owners, Admins, Managers, and Members are billable; taxes are extra and refunds are generally unavailable. Kiosk seats cost $0.99/$0.79 Basic, $1.49/$1.19 Standard, $1.99/$1.59 Pro, or $2.99/$2.39 Enterprise monthly/annual per kiosk seat.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Clockify, track time, approve entries, and generate basic client or project reports. The hard boundary is many platforms, team administration, kiosks, scheduling, and hosted scale, plus ubiquitous capture, coaching, and team workflow.
coreLoopDIY: Track time and focused sessions, approve entries, generate basic client or project reports, review patterns locally, and export a transparent activity record.
requirements: optional accessibility permission for app-name tracking
whatYouLose: many platforms, team administration, kiosks, scheduling, and hosted scale
moatNotes: ubiquitous capture, coaching, and team workflow
ongoingBurden: idle detection, permissions, app metadata, privacy, notifications, sync, reports, integrations, and backups
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Clockify because the timer is simple, but people pay for frictionless capture and a history they trust enough to invoice or change habits from. The recurring cost buys idle detection, permissions, app metadata, privacy, notifications, sync, reports, integrations, and backups, not just the visible interface.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Basic plan and a personal desktop tracker DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Clockify in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, SQLite, and optional OS accessibility APIs; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: track time and focused sessions, approve entries, generate basic client or project reports, review patterns locally, and export a transparent activity record.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create one-click start and stop, manual entries, idle detection, tags, projects, and notes.
Keep any application-name tracking opt-in and never record window contents or keystrokes.
Add Pomodoro-style focus sessions, break reminders, and an optional allowlist blocker.
Provide daily, weekly, project, and category reports with editable corrections.
Export CSV and JSON and make the underlying event log inspectable.
Add automatic local backups and a privacy screen explaining every collected field.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out employee surveillance.
Deliberately leave out payroll and billing automation.
Deliberately leave out cross-device blocking and behavioral coaching services.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
